segments: and when they were about {OCR?} to celebrate the feast of Hosannas (Palm Sunday),
and knew that the Arabs (Muslims) were prepared to trouble them,
they sent and summoned to their aid certain of the Christian Tatars (Mongols) who were near.
And when they arrived, they placed crosses upon the heads of their spears,
and the Metropolitan of the Nestorians went out with all the people,
with those Tatar horsemen before them.
And when they drew near before the fortress,
crowds of the Arabs assembled,
and they took up stones and stoned the Tatars and the Christians.
And their assembly was scattered,
and each one of the Christians fled in every direction;
and after this they remained for days without daring to go outside.
And this also brought distress upon the Christians in every place.
And in this year, Khawaja Nasir, the Persian philosopher, passed away,
a man renowned, famous, and preeminent in all branches of wisdom,
especially in these mathematical sciences.
He constructed observational instruments
and large brass spheres (armillary spheres),
which were more marvelous than those
that Ptolemy set up in Alexandria;
and he observed and corrected
the course of the stars.
And a multitude of wise men from various lands gathered to him in Maragha, the city of Azerbaijan.
And because the endowments of all the mosques and colleges of Baghdad and Assyria were under his authority,
and from them he would give stipends to the teachers and students who were with him,
at this time, when he went to Baghdad to visit those places,
in that same Baghdad he died.
And some reported that he was poisoned.
For they wrote many books:
commentaries on logic, and on natural and divine learning (physics and metaphysics).
And he also edited Euclid and the Almagest with great thoroughness.
And he also has an Ethics in the Persian tongue,
in which he expounded the words of Plato and of Aristotle on practical philosophy.
For he held fast to the opinion of the ancient philosophers,
and vigorously opposed their adversaries in his writing.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and eighty-six
[1586] of the Greeks (1274-1275 AD),
in the month of the Prior Kanun (December),
certain evildoers went in Mosul
and knocked at the door of a certain Jewish silversmith at night.
And when he answered them and said to them:
"What do you want?" they said to him:
"We are youths,
and we have come to you that you might give us provision (money)."
